title: How David Goggins callouses his mind: suffering, repetition, and no finish line (JRE #1212)
summary: Goggins explains how he used brutal, repeated physical work to build mental armor, face his past, and stop making excuses. He stresses doing hard things daily, training without external motivation, and accepting that there is no finish line. He is candid about his flaws, injuries and procrastination.

principles.text: Use training to build calluses on your mind, not just your body.
principles.quote: i saw working out as a way for me to build calluses on my mind i had to callous over the victim's mentality

principles.text: Repeat the things you don't want to do until your mind is armored for hard times.
principles.quote: through repetition of things you don't want to do you develop mental like like an armor for your mind

principles.text: Hold yourself accountable in the mirror and go where the pain is, because that's where answers are.
principles.quote: over there was me looking in the mirror over there was me being accountable for all these things that went through my life

principles.text: There is no finish line or golden retirement; keep finding your new 100 percent.
principles.quote: there's no end my friend there's no end

principles.text: Train without music or outside motivation, so you can fire yourself up from within.
principles.quote: what do you do when you have no external motivation it's about the internal

principles.text: You leave untapped potential on the table; pain management shows what you're capable of.
principles.quote: what have i been leaving on the table right i've been leaving so much on the [ __ ] table for pain
